title: Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing — Returned Payments
content:
Payments operations bulletin for Ridgeline Home Improvement Financing accounts.

**Rule.** A payment the bank returns unpaid is added back to the balance on the return date, naming the payment, and draws the plan's returned payment fee once. A returned payment does not count as paid, so the period's late fee rules apply to it as if it had never posted. When an account reaches the stated number of returned payments in the preceding 365 days, autopay is suspended and the autopay rate discount stops from the next statement period; the customer may enroll again once a later payment posts without being returned.

## Effects of one returned payment

| Effect | Detail |
|---|---|
| Balance | The returned amount is added back on the return date, naming the payment returned |
| Fee | The plan's returned payment fee, once |
| Status of the payment | Not paid; the late fee rules of its statement period apply as if it had never posted |

## Autopay suspension

The count is the returned payments on the account in the rolling 365 calendar days ending on the handling date. When it reaches the plan's suspension count:

1. autopay is suspended;
2. the autopay rate discount stops from the next statement period;
3. the customer may enroll again once a later payment posts without being returned.

## Hypothetical case

On a plan whose suspension count is 2, an account with one returned payment eight months ago and a second returned today has 2 returns in the preceding 365 days: autopay is suspended and the autopay rate discount stops from the next statement period. A return fourteen months ago would fall outside the 365 days and would not count. The timeline is illustrative.
